newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans to allow treasury stock system.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans to allow treasury stock system.

text.p: Taiwan's securities watchdog said on Thursday it planned to revise regulations to allow companies to hold treasury stocks in order to raise funds by issuing warrants or convertible bonds.

"We held a meeting on Wednesday with related government offices, and all agreed that it's feasible to launch the treasury stock system," a spokeswoman at the Securities and Futures Commission told Reuters.
"The treasury stock system will help local firms raise funds by issuing warrants or convertible bonds," she said by telephone.

Currently, local firms which have issued convertible bonds must issue certificates of conversion to investors first, then conduct rights issues or other methods to accumulate needed stocks for conversion, she said.
"The conversion usually would take more than half a year, wasting time and reducing investor willingness to hold the convertible bonds," she said.
"But with the treasury stock, companies which have issued convertibles, will have stocks available for immediate conversion, thus adding investors' holding interests," she said.
The commission said its proposal would revise the Company Law to allow companies to issue warrants based on their own shares -- a move that the current law bans.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange said in June that 31 listed firms qualified for warrant issues, the latest instrument to be pioneered in Taiwan's liberalising financial system.

Only local and foreign banks or securities brokerages with T$3 billion in registered capital could issue warrants on qualified shares, but listed firms are not allowed to issue warrants based on their own stocks.
Taiwan's first warrant issue was expected to start by the end of July, officials said.
